bodyHTML:
Keymaps:

  • <C-Left> / <C-Right> like in Insert mode, respecting vim.bo.iskeyword
  • <Home> / <End> like in Insert mode (overrides move_start, see comment)
  • <C-S-Left> / <C-S-Right> similar to <C-Left> / <C-Right> in Cmdline
pick-motions.mp4 
local run_keys = function(keys, rep)
  vim.api.nvim_input(string.rep(keys, rep or 1))
end

local move_caret = function(next_caret)
  local caret = MiniPick.get_picker_state().caret
  local query = MiniPick.get_picker_query()
  next_caret = math.max(1, math.min(next_caret, #query + 1))
  local move = next_caret - caret
  run_keys(move >= 0 and "<Right>" or "<Left>", math.abs(move))
end

require("mini.pick").setup({
  mappings = {
    -- Easy
    caret_start = {
      char = "<Home>",
      func = function()
        move_caret(1)
      end,
    },
    caret_end = {
      char = "<End>",
      func = function()
        -- TIP: You can also use `math.huge` instead
        move_caret(#MiniPick.get_picker_query() + 1)
      end,
    },
    -- Medium
    -- Like <C-Left>/<C-Right> in Cmdline, but skip spaces
    prev_before_space = {
      char = "<C-S-Left>",
      func = function()
        local query_str = table.concat(MiniPick.get_picker_query())
        local caret = MiniPick.get_picker_state().caret
        local search_str = string.sub(query_str, 1, caret - 1)
        local word_start = string.find(search_str, "%S+%s*$")
        move_caret(word_start or 1)
      end,
    },
    next_before_space = {
      char = "<C-S-Right>",
      func = function()
        local query_str = table.concat(MiniPick.get_picker_query())
        local caret = MiniPick.get_picker_state().caret
        local word_end = string.find(query_str, "%f[%s]", caret + 1)
        move_caret(word_end or #query_str + 1)
      end,
    },
    -- Hard
    -- Like <C-Left>/<C-Right> in Insert mode, vim.bo.iskeyword
    prev_word = {
      char = "<C-Left>",
      func = function()
        local query_str = table.concat(MiniPick.get_picker_query())
        local caret = MiniPick.get_picker_state().caret
        -- TIP: To avoid recompiling regex on each key press, move it outside the `func`
        -- NOTE: ((not keyword and not space)+ OR keyword+)space*$
        local regex = vim.regex([=[\([^[:keyword:][:space:]]\+\|\k\+\)\s*$]=])
        local from, _ = regex:match_str(string.sub(query_str, 1, caret - 1))
        local prev_word_start = from and from + 1 or nil
        move_caret(prev_word_start or 1)
      end,
    },
    next_word = {
      char = "<C-Right>",
      func = function()
        local query_str = table.concat(MiniPick.get_picker_query())
        local caret = MiniPick.get_picker_state().caret
        -- NOTE: ^((not keyword and not space)+ OR keyword+)space*
        local regex = vim.regex([=[^\([^[:keyword:][:space:]]\+\|\k\+\)\s*]=])
        local _, to = regex:match_str(string.sub(query_str, caret))
        local next_word_start = to and to + caret or nil
        move_caret(next_word_start or #query_str + 1)
      end,
    },
    -- stylua: ignore start
    caret_start_alt = { char = "<C-a>", func = function() run_keys("<Home>") end },
    caret_end_alt = { char = "<C-e>", func = function() run_keys("<End>") end },
    move_down_alt = { char = "<C-j>", func = function() run_keys("<C-n>") end },
    move_up_alt = { char = "<C-k>", func = function() run_keys("<C-p>") end },
  },
})

reply_data.body:
At the moment, I don't think so.

- `<Home>` is already supported and is an alternative to `move_start` action.
- The `<End>` is the same as `<Home><Up>` and is not really useful when it comes to navigating through matches.
- `<C-Right>` and `<C-left>` is a bit too much. Especially since it requires 'iskeyword' support, which is also rather ambiguous. Since it can be a buffer-local option, picker's behavior will depend on the current buffer. Which is somewhat unintuitive. Always using global option is doable, but may be a bit unintuitive for people who are not really aware about global/local options.

    One extra problem here is that query technically can contain not only single letters, but whole words. So full "word" navigation is not always possible since caret can be placed only in between query entries.

reply_data.body:
I still believe it should work the same way it does in Insert mode. For me, that’s a feature that has to be there, one way or another.

1. Using `PageUp` for `move_start` makes more sense to me.
2. Since `vim.bo.iskeyword` is a buffer-local option, it can be changed in `MiniPickStart` because the picker focuses on the main window. It will use the `vim.o.iskeyword` option by default but can be overridden in the autocmd with `vim.bo.iskeyword` (in theory).

These keymaps might not seem very useful at first glance, but they’re actually quite handy. I understand that refining helps to some extent—one word at a time—but these keymaps will not only make multiword searching much easier, they also allow you to change already typed "code" in the search. Imagine you’ve typed `vim.print("name")` and want to change `vim.print` to `vim.notify`. Wouldn’t it be easier to press `<C-Left>` a few times followed by `<C-w>`?

Also, regarding refining, is there a way to jump back to the previous refinement?

> 1. Using `PageUp` for `move_start` makes more sense to me.

`<PageUp>` is more like `scroll_up` action.

> Wouldn’t it be easier to press `<C-Left>` a few times followed by `<C-w>`?

Easier - probably. Doing something that is not currently possible - no. Expanding 'mini.pick' only for something very high leverage is a high priority right now. Mostly due to the module's size.

> Also, regarding refining, is there a way to jump back to the previous refinement?

I am afraid, no. That would add memory footprint and code complexity. And there is no good default key for that which is universally supported enough.

> `<PageUp>` is more like a `scroll_up` action.

Makes sense. But even in normal mode, `<Home>` and `<End>` don’t jump to the first and last columns.

> That would add memory footprint and code complexity.

I don’t think memory footprint is an issue unless all entries are saved—saving only the query should be enough. But I haven’t looked at the code, so it’s really stupid for me to argue.

> And there is no good default key for that which is universally supported enough.

I would use "Control/Alt + Arrow" keys.

I guess implementing such a feature would only make sense if at least a few people needed it, not just me. I just hope it doesn’t get thrown into the "not to do" bucket, but at least into the "maybe to do" list. Personally, I can always keep these mappings in my own configuration.

Note that `<Home>` is a [built-in mapping](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/9087880da9ed1e5b06a28b75b4424fd8218bd189/doc/mini-pick.txt#L534) that will always be there as an alternative to `move_start` action. So mapping it to `move_caret(1)` will probably be ambiguous.
